page.overview:
Who is Dorzhi?

Belonging to one of the nomadic Si Wong clans that roamed the Si Wong Desert's Northern Plains, Dorzhi was cared for by an elder relative during his youth. At the time, the region suffered under a decades-long drought and the local clans mostly survived by pledging loyalty to the Earth Kingdom. He was an earthbender and learned how to control a sand-sailer when was still young.

One day in the 130s AG, two sand-sailers made a stop at the Si Wong meeting place where Dorzhi and his elder were staying at the time. The elder greeted the newcomers, embracing Tsetseg, a fellow tribeswoman who worked as an Earth Kingdom Army guide. When Tsetseg revealed that they had come to recruit sandbenders for an anti-raider operation, the elder initially claimed that no benders were present at the meeting place. Militia leader Bai Yin Du immediately realized that this was a lie due to the presence of other sand-sailers at the locality, threatening the elder. Seeing this, Dorzhi rushed out of a nearby building, revealing himself as a sanbender and volunteering to join the mission. Bai Yin happily accepted him and declared that he would receive a water ration for his clan after one month of service. Despite the elder's protests, Dorzhi subsequently accompanied the militia into the desert.

The group continued their journey until evening, when they set up camp at a small stone overcrop. They were surprised by a rattle jackal which promptly attacked, biting Dorzhi's right arm and injecting its venom. The rest of the group managed to fend off the creature and they fled onto their sand-sailers, returning to the open desert. Kya attempted to heal Dorzhi but discovered that her waterbending was blocked. Another militia member, Anwat, suggested muri bean leaves as an alternate treatment. While Dorzhi suffered growing pain and fever due to the venom, Anwat managed to gather some leaves from the surrounding desert. The group was able to create an ad hoc antidote and successfully cared for the young sandbender, though the boy remained deeply weakened. On the next day, Bai Yin ordered Anwat to bring Dorzhi to Liyuan for further treatment, while she, Kya, and Tsetseg continued their journey.

Dorzhi was later discharged from the Liyuan militia and happily reunited with his elder, assuring her that his arm "was not too bad" as he had received quick medical aid from the others.
